The KV-Cache, Made Concrete.zh: 把 KV 缓存讲明白

Every token an LLM generates re-reads ev.zh:
LLM 每生成一个词元，都要重新读取此前所有词元的 key 与 value。
      将它们缓存起来是必需的——而缓存很快就会远超权重本身。
      拖动下方的模型、上下文与批量滑块，观察 KV 缓存超过参数的那一瞬间。
      这正是“LLM 推理受内存限制，而非受算力限制”的原因。
Every token an LLM generates re-reads ev.src:
Every token an LLM generates re-reads every key and value from all previous
      tokens. Caching them is mandatory — and the cache quickly dwarfs the
      weights. Slide the model, the context, and the batch below and watch the
      moment the KV-cache overtakes the parameters. This is why
      “LLM inference is memory-bound, not compute-bound.”

Why the cache has to exist.src: Why the cache has to exist

To predict token $t{+}1$, self-attention.zh:
为预测词元 $t{+}1$，自注意力会把当前的 query 与此前@@T0@@每一个@@T1@@词元的
      key 进行比较，并按权重混合它们的 value：
To predict token $t{+}1$, self-attention.src: To predict token $t{+}1$, self-attention compares the current query against the key of every earlier token and mixes in their values:

The keys $k_i$ and values $v_i$ of past.zh:
过去词元的 key $k_i$ 与 value $v_i$ 永不改变。若在每一步都重新计算它们，
      会使生成的时间代价无谓地变为 $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$。因此我们把它们@@T0@@缓存@@T1@@起来：
      一个词元处理完毕后，它的 $k$ 与 $v$（在每一层、每个注意力头中）就被存储并永久复用。
      这种权衡——用内存换取算力——正是自回归解码得以快速的原因，
      也正是它@@T2@@受内存限制@@T3@@的原因。每个新词元都要把整个缓存从 HBM 中读回；
      相对于所搬运的字节数，其中的算术运算微不足道。
The keys $k_i$ and values $v_i$ of past.src: The keys $k_i$ and values $v_i$ of past tokens never change. Recomputing them at each step would make generation cost $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ in time for no reason. So we cache them: after a token is processed, its $k$ and $v$ (in every layer, every head) are stored and re-used forever. That trade — spend memory to save compute — is what makes autoregressive decoding fast, and what makes it memory-bound. Every new token reads the entire cache back out of HBM; the arithmetic is trivial next to the bytes moved.

The one formula that governs everything.src: The one formula that governs everything

$L$ &mdash; number of transformer layers.src: $L$ — number of transformer layers (the cache is stored once per layer).

Multiply by the context length and the batch size (concurrent sequences) and

      $\;\text{bytes}_{\text{total}} = \text{bytes}_{\text{token}} \cdot \text{context} \cdot \text{batch}.$
      Nothing here depends on the size of the MLP or the vocabulary — the cache
      is a pure function of the attention shape. Time to make it move.

The chart plots two things against context length: the flat model weights and the rising KV-cache. Where the cache line overtakes the weights is the memory cliff — past it, your GPU is spending more on remembering the conversation than on the model itself.

@@T0@@Try this.@@T1@@ Load @@T2@@Llama-3.src: Try this. Load Llama-3 70B, then drag batch size up from 1. At batch 1 the cache is a footnote next to the 130 GB of weights. But KV scales with every concurrent user, so by batch 32 the orange area has climbed past the blue band — the same model now needs multiple GPUs just to hold conversations in flight. Now switch the same model to MHA: with $n_{kv}$ jumping from 8 to 64, the cliff arrives $8\times$ sooner. That single design choice is why every modern model uses GQA.

PagedAttention: stop reserving what you.zh: PagedAttention：不要再预留你用不到的内存
PagedAttention: stop reserving what you.src: PagedAttention: stop reserving what you don't use

There is a second, subtler waste. A naiv.zh:
还有第二重更隐蔽的浪费。朴素的服务器不知道回复会有多长，
      于是会为每条序列的事先按最大上下文@@T0@@预留@@T1@@一块连续缓冲区。
      多数回复都很短，因此这块缓冲区大部分都空着——即@@T2@@内部碎片@@T3@@。
      vLLM 的 PagedAttention 借用了操作系统的分页思路：内存是
      一池固定大小的@@T4@@块@@T5@@，序列只在增长时才抓取新的块。
      在两种方式之间切换，观察被浪费（斜线填充）的内存如何坍缩。
There is a second, subtler waste. A naiv.src: There is a second, subtler waste. A naive server does not know how long a reply will be, so it reserves a contiguous buffer for the maximum context of every sequence up front. Most replies are short, so most of that buffer sits empty — internal fragmentation. vLLM's PagedAttention borrows the operating-system trick of paging: memory is a pool of small fixed blocks, and a sequence grabs blocks only as it grows. Toggle between the two and watch the wasted (hatched) memory collapse.

Each cell is one block. Solid = tokens a.zh: 每个单元格为一个块。实心 = 实际存储的词元；斜线填充 = 已预留但为空。
Each cell is one block. Solid = tokens a.src: Each cell is one block. Solid = tokens actually stored; hatched = reserved but empty.

@@T0@@Why it matters.@@T1@@ Naive reserv.zh:
@@T0@@为何重要。@@T1@@ 朴素预留常常浪费
      60–80% 的 KV 内存。通过分页，vLLM 把利用率保持在接近
      100%，这意味着同一块显卡上能容纳远更多的序列——

@@T0@@Why it matters.@@T1@@ Naive reserv.src: Why it matters. Naive reservation routinely wastes 60–80% of KV memory. By paging, vLLM keeps utilisation near 100%, which means far more sequences fit on the same card — higher throughput from the exact same hardware. Smaller blocks waste less at the tail but add bookkeeping; 16–128 tokens per block is the usual sweet spot.

Every term in $2 \cdot L \cdot n_{kv} \cdot d_h \cdot p$ is a lever, and the
      field has pulled each of them:

Let several query heads share one key/va.zh:
让若干个查询头共享一个 key/value 头。GQA(8) 把 $n_{kv}$
        从 64 降到 8——缓存缩小 $8\times$，而质量损失可忽略不计。
        MQA 则以单个 KV 头把它推向极致。
Let several query heads share one key/va.src:
Let several query heads share one key/value head. GQA(8) cuts $n_{kv}$
        from 64 to 8 — an $8\times$ smaller cache with negligible quality loss.
        MQA takes it to the extreme with a single KV head.

Store keys and values in 8 bits instead.zh:
把 key 与 value 用 8 位而非 16 位存储。字节数减半，
        通常无需付出代价；偶尔会有轻微精度波动。在实验台中切换它，
        悬崖会向右移动两倍远。
Store keys and values in 8 bits instead.src:
Store keys and values in 8 bits instead of 16. Halves the bytes, often
        for free; occasionally a small accuracy nudge. Toggle it in the Lab and the
        cliff moves twice as far right.

Allocate KV in fixed blocks instead of o.zh:
以固定大小的块分配 KV，而非为每条序列分配一整块连续缓冲区。
        没有碎片，没有超额预留——这正是 vLLM 高吞吐的核心技巧。
Allocate KV in fixed blocks instead of o.src:
Allocate KV in fixed blocks instead of one giant contiguous buffer per
        sequence. No fragmentation, no over-reservation — the trick at the
        heart of vLLM's throughput.

@@T0@@Takeaway.@@T1@@ The KV-cache is th.zh:
@@T0@@要点。@@T1@@ KV 缓存是长上下文与高并发所隐含的代价。
      其规模完全由注意力形状决定 —
      $2 \cdot L \cdot n_{kv} \cdot d_h \cdot p$ — 且它既随每段对话的长度增长，
      也随同时进行的对话数量增长。大规模部署 LLM，粗略地说，
      就是把这一个数字压小的艺术。
@@T0@@Takeaway.@@T1@@ The KV-cache is th.src: Takeaway. The KV-cache is the hidden tax on long context and high concurrency. Its size is set entirely by the attention shape — $2 \cdot L \cdot n_{kv} \cdot d_h \cdot p$ — and it grows with both the length of each conversation and the number of them at once. Serving LLMs at scale is, to a first approximation, the art of keeping this number small.

meta.title: 把 KV 缓存讲明白
meta.tagline: LLM 推理为何受内存限制——以每个词元的兆字节数来衡量。
meta.summary: 为什么一个 70B 的 LLM 即使批量为 1 也需要 80GB 的 GPU？不是权重，而是 KV 缓存。拖动模型规模、上下文长度、批量大小与头共享方式（GQA），观察缓存规模如何占据主导。再切换 PagedAttention，看 vLLM 如何夺回容量。
highlights: 参数量、层数、上下文、批量的滑块——实时显示 KV 缓存的总 GB 数。
在 MHA、GQA(8) 与 MQA 之间切换——观察各自的内存悬崖。
PagedAttention 演示：连续分配与分页分配对比，碎片回收。
